title: Net Promoter Score: Should Small Businesses Track It?

facts.fact: The page says NPS asks customers to rate how likely they are to recommend the business on a 0 to 10 scale.
facts.quote: how likely is the customer to recommend your business on a 0 to 10 scale?

facts.fact: The page defines Promoters as customers who score 9 to 10 on the NPS question.
The page defines Passives as customers who score 7 to 8 on the NPS question.
The page defines Detractors as customers who score 0 to 6 on the NPS question.
The page gives the NPS formula as percentage of Promoters minus percentage of Detractors.
The page states that Passives are not counted in the NPS formula.
facts.quote: Passives do not count in the formula.

facts.fact: According to Ringly (a third-party source cited by the page), NPS explains 20% to 60% of the variation in organic growth rates in most industries.
facts.quote: NPS explains 20% to 60% of the variation in organic growth rates

facts.fact: According to Ringly (a third-party source cited by the page), NPS leaders outgrow rivals by a factor greater than two times.
facts.quote: NPS leaders outgrow rivals by a factor greater than two times

facts.fact: According to Ringly (a third-party source cited by the page), companies with an NPS of 75 or higher see at least 13% higher Customer Lifetime Value.
facts.quote: companies with an NPS of 75 or higher see at least 13% higher Customer Lifetime Value
